Brand red rules

Brand red #EE0700 is kept exactly (header colour on the live site). Measured contrast: black on red is 4.67:1; white on red is 4.50:1, an AA pass by 0.0008 and not AAA for either. Because the white margin is that thin, anti-aliasing or any opacity can tip it under.

  • Default to black text (--color-on-brand) on red.
  • White on red only for large or bold text, never for small body text or thin icons.
  • Red text or links on light surfaces use --color-brand-text, a darker red. Plain #EE0700 on white is also only 4.50:1.
  • Never place red text on the red surface, or pale text on amber.

Type

Interim stack: Poppins then the system UI stack. The final font is decided later from Google fonts and default system fonts; whichever is chosen is self-hosted as a subset woff2 with font-display: swap. Base is 16px/24px; sizes are rem so user font settings and 400% zoom work.

3xl 2.25rem, page title

2xl 1.75rem, section heading

xl 1.375rem, card heading

lg 1.125rem, lede

base 1rem, body text on a 1.5 line height

sm 0.875rem, secondary and captions

xs 0.75rem, legal only; never for essential information

Theme config mapping

Core colours are exposed in config.json so the store admin can adjust them; node scripts/generate-design-tokens.mjs reports where config defaults differ from these tokens. Contrast is re-checked at build, so a bad admin choice must also be caught by the in-theme guard (to be specified in the implementation brief).

Accessibility playbook

Baseline WCAG 2.2 AA, with AAA adopted where it costs little (the contrast table marks AAA per pair). Accessibility is a build rule, not a review step: artistic intent is preserved by tuning tokens, not by relaxing the rule.

Fixes carried over from the live site

Live site todayNew theme
No <main> landmarkOne <main id="main"> per page, focus target of the skip link.
No skip linkFirst focusable element: "Skip to content"; visible on focus.
H1 rendered at 0px on the home pageExactly one visible <h1> per page; no visually hidden headline hacks.
11 <footer> elementsOne page <footer>; groups inside use <section> or <nav aria-label>.
Images without altEvery <img> has alt; decorative images use alt="". Checked by npm run check-bible for this document.

Structure

  • Landmarks: header, nav (each labelled), main, footer. Heading levels descend without skipping.
  • Links are links, actions are buttons. Whole-card links expose one name, not the image alt plus the title twice.
  • Page title and lang="en-AU" on every page.

Interaction

  • Focus is always visible: 3px ring using --color-focus, offset 2px, 3:1 against both themes (checked).
  • Focus is never hidden under sticky headers: sticky elements set scroll-padding-top and the page offsets anchors (WCAG 2.2 focus not obscured).
  • Target size at least 24x24 CSS px (AA); aim for 44px on touch controls. Buttons in this bible are 44px tall.
  • Everything works by keyboard; no keyboard traps; menus and dialogs return focus to their trigger.
  • No drag-only interaction (gallery swipe has buttons). No gesture timing.
  • Do not require re-entering information in the same checkout flow; show errors next to fields and in a summary.

Forms

  • Every control has a visible <label>; placeholders are never the label.
  • Required and format hints are text, linked with aria-describedby.
  • Errors: plain-language message, tied to the field, announced once via role="alert" or a live summary; colour is never the only cue.
  • autocomplete tokens on name, address, email, phone and card fields.

Colour, themes and motion

  • Light follows the design, dark follows prefers-color-scheme, and a toggle stores the visitor's choice. Without JS the page follows the OS.
  • Every token pair is contrast-checked in both themes at build time; AA failures fail the build.
  • prefers-reduced-motion: reduce sets motion tokens to 0ms; carousels do not autoplay, and any motion over 5 seconds has a pause control.
  • Information is never conveyed by colour alone (stock status, errors, selected variant use text or icons too).

Test checklist

CheckHow
Keyboard onlyTab through the page: order, focus ring, no traps, skip link works.
Screen readerNVDA or VoiceOver pass on landmarks, headings, forms, dynamic updates.
Zoom and reflow200% text and 400% zoom (320 CSS px wide): no horizontal scroll, no clipped content.
No JavaScriptBrowse, filter, add to cart and reach checkout with scripts disabled.
Reduced motion and darkEmulate both; layouts and focus stay intact.
Automatednpm run design (tokens, structure) plus an axe or Lighthouse accessibility run per page.

Asset policy

Embed, do not link. Nothing the page needs at runtime is fetched from a third-party CDN. This applies to icons, fonts, JavaScript libraries and images where the platform allows.

What the live site loads from elsewhere, and the replacement

Live site dependencyNew theme
Font Awesome 6 via cdnjs.cloudflare.comStatic inline SVG at build time, only the icons used.
Poppins via fonts.googleapis.comSelf-hosted subset woff2 (latin), font-display: swap, system fallback stack. Final font choice later.
PapaThemes script and theme codeReplaced by this theme's own templates and islands. No vendor script.
websitespeedycdn.b-cdn.netDropped. Caching and image sizing handled by the platform CDN and srcset.
GTM, PostHog, Bing, MailchimpOut of scope here; handled in the marketing brief. The site must work with all of them absent.
BigCommerce platform CDN (images, checkout SDK)Platform-provided and unavoidable for product images and checkout; the only external origins allowed, listed in the performance budget.

Icons

  • Packs: Lucide, Heroicons and Font Awesome (free set) are all permitted, chosen per icon for fit, one pack per concept.
  • Delivery: server-rendered inline <svg>, currentColor, aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false" unless the icon is the only content, in which case the control carries a text label or aria-label.
  • No icon fonts. No sprite sheet request by default.
  • Sizing in em so icons scale with text; stroke icons use a 2px stroke.

JavaScript libraries

  • Bundle through the build; no <script src="https://...">.
  • Prefer no library: native <details>, CSS scroll snap, popover and the platform before adding a dependency. New packages need approval.
  • React runs only inside islands (see the islands and data map).

Images

  • Every image has width and height (no layout shift), alt text per the voice section, loading="lazy" below the fold and fetchpriority="high" on the LCP image only.
  • Responsive srcset and sizes from the platform image CDN; modern formats where available.
  • Brand images are shipped in the theme (assets/img); product images come from the catalogue.
  • Text is real text, never baked into an image (hero headlines, promo banners).

Performance budget

All numbers here are proposals to be confirmed against a real baseline measurement of the live site and the first built pages.

Targets (mobile, mid-range device, 4G)

MetricTargetWhy
LCP2.5 s or better at p75Hero or first product image is static HTML with fetchpriority="high".
CLS0.1 or betterReserved image sizes, no late-injected banners above content.
INP200 ms or betterSmall islands, no large hydration on load.
Requests in flightOne batched GraphQL request per page for island dataServer prefetch plus a single deduped client query.

Weight budget per page type (compressed)

PageHTML + CSSJavaScriptFontsNotes
Home60 KB30 KB40 KBStatic content; islands for tabs, theme toggle, mini-cart.
Category / search70 KB40 KB40 KBFilters work as links and forms; the island only enhances.
Product70 KB50 KB40 KBVariant selector island and gallery enhancer.
Cart50 KB25 KB40 KBForm posts work without JS.

Allowed external origins

  • BigCommerce image CDN (product and platform images) and the BigCommerce checkout.
  • Everything else is first party. Tracking and marketing origins are decided in the marketing brief and must load only after consent, deferred, never blocking render.

Rules

  • Critical CSS is inline per page type; the rest is a single cached stylesheet.
  • No render-blocking third-party anything. No web font blocking text.
  • Islands hydrate on visibility or interaction unless the page is unusable without them.
  • Run Lighthouse (npm run lighthouse) per page type before release and record results.

Content and brand voice

Derived from the live site's copy on 2026-11-23. Online Workwear is an Australian-owned, family-operated uniform and workwear supplier serving tradies, businesses and teams.

Tone

  • Straight and practical. Say what the garment does and who it suits. No hype words.
  • Trustworthy and local. Lead with Australian owned, Australian-based service, standing behind quality.
  • Helpful to teams. Make ordering for a business feel easy: no minimum orders, free embroidery set-up over a threshold.
  • Australian English (colour, organisation). Plain words; short sentences.

Copy rules

RuleExample
Button text says the action"Add to cart", "Choose colour", never "Click here".
Links say where they go"Hi Vis workwear", not "Read more".
Prices and offers are text"Spend $299 and save 10%". Thresholds come from theme settings, not a baked image.
Errors tell the fix"Enter an email like name@example.com", not "Invalid input".
Sentence case headings"Popular categories", not "POPULAR CATEGORIES" (use CSS only if the case is purely visual).
Spell out specs"UPF 50+ with mesh vent panels" keeps the live site's practical detail.

Imagery

  • Real people in real work settings, clothing clearly visible; hi-vis and flame-resistant ranges shown in use.
  • Consistent product shots on a plain background for grids, one crop ratio per grid.
  • Alt text describes the product (colour, style) for products, the meaning for promo images, and is empty for decoration.

Structured content

  • Keep the Organization JSON-LD from the live site; add Product and BreadcrumbList on product and category pages.
  • Reviews are real quotes with attribution; never fabricated or rewritten.

Decoration and branding copy (embroidery, printing) and marketing copy: second pass, separate briefs.

Facet filters and sort

Colour

No JS: a GET form that reloads the category with the chosen filters in the URL ("Apply filters" visible). Facet links are crawlable.

Size

Page spec: Product

The product page is where most of the interactive weight lives, and where the no-JS fallback matters most: a visitor can always choose options and add to cart with plain form controls.

LayoutMobile: single column, add to cart after options. Desktop: gallery left, buy box right, sticky only if it never obscures focused fields.
ComponentsBreadcrumbs, gallery, price and badges, variant selector, quantity and add to cart, FAQ-style details for specs, reviews, product cards.
DataServer renders product, options and initial variant data. The variant island receives the product id and storefront token from the template (existing colour-size.tsx pattern) and issues one batched availability query for all option combinations, shared with the gallery and price islands.
No JSNative radio inputs for every option; add to cart is a form POST; gallery is a stacked or scroll-snap list; specs are <details>.

Decoration and branding step (logo placement, embroidery, print options) on the product page: second pass; this layout reserves the space between options and add to cart.

Page spec: Cart and checkout entry

The cart is a plain server-rendered form. Checkout itself is the platform's hosted checkout and is out of scope for restyling here, but the handoff must be clear and accessible.

Header, breadcrumbs h1 Your cart (n items) Line items: image, name and options, price, quantity, remove Coupon / gift certificate (details) Shipping estimate (form) Summary: subtotal, savings (spend-and-save tiers), total Checkout button (primary) + continue shopping link Footer
ComponentsButtons, form controls, price, promo banner (tier progress as text, "Add $X more to save 15%"), mini cart (hidden on this page).
DataServer renders the cart. Quantity updates are form posts; with JS an island updates the line and summary with one request and replaces the region.
No JSQuantity input with an "Update" button; remove is a button in the line's form; coupon and shipping estimate are forms; the Checkout button is a link to the platform checkout.
StatesEmpty cart (message, link to categories), updating (aria-busy), item unavailable (explained), error with a retry that keeps what the visitor typed.
A11yLine items in a table or list with clear names for each button ("Remove Hi-vis polo, size M"); the total and tier progress are text; updates announced politely; no timeouts.
Checkout handoffThe button states that checkout opens the secure checkout; the page the platform serves is kept visually consistent where its settings allow (colours, logo).

Decoration details on cart line items (artwork preview, set-up fees): second pass.

Islands and data map

HBX renders as much as possible statically. A component becomes an island only when it needs state or live data that cannot be a link, a form or CSS. Every island ships with static markup that already works, and fails safe: a script error leaves the static page usable.

Data contract

  1. Server prefetch. Page data comes from the template's front matter (the platform's GraphQL data) and is rendered into HTML. Nothing paints from a client request.
  2. One batched client query. All islands on a page register their data needs with a shared client module that merges them into one GraphQL request per tick, dedupes identical fields and caches by key. Targets: at most one request in flight on load, and none when the server already provided the data.
  3. Defer and idle. Islands hydrate on visibility or interaction; only islands needed to use the page hydrate on load.
  4. Fail safe. Each island defines loading, error and empty states, a timeout, and a way back to the static behaviour (form submit, link).
  5. Token handling. The storefront token is passed from the template as a prop (as VariantEnhancer already does); no secrets in the bundle.
